name: The Parasol Pine of Parc de l'Orangerie

location.address: Parc de l'Orangerie, Avenue de l'Europe, 67000 Strasbourg

access: Free, public park (Parc de l'Orangerie, Strasbourg's oldest public park, laid out in 1692)
transport: Tram E, Droits de l'Homme stop, short walk into the park
verify_notes: City register entry (Ville et Eurometropole de Strasbourg, 'Lieux - Arbres remarquables', Licence Ouverte/Etalab, dataset fetched 2026-08-13) gives tree-level coordinates and this description, translated: remarkable for the height and width of its trunk, with a parasol-shaped crown and a tortuous (gnarled/twisted) trunk; ivy grows along the trunk, noted as a distinctive feature. Species notes from the same register: Scots pine is widespread across Europe and Asia, can reach 10-30m (up to 40m) and can live 500-600 years -- these are species-level facts, not a measured age for this individual, so age is left blank rather than inferred. SINGLE SOURCE: only the city's own register was found describing this specific tree. Checked and came up empty for an independent second source: French Wikipedia's Parc de l'Orangerie article does not name individual trees (only mentions the orangery's three orange trees and the plane-tree avenue); the University of Strasbourg herbarium's flora page for the park lists species present (Acer, Platanus, Prunus, Laburnum etc.) but not individual remarkable specimens; monumentaltrees.com's Orangerie page could not be viewed this pass (site blocks automated fetches per its own anti-scraping measure, needs a live browser session per project rules); the Collectivite europeenne d'Alsace's separate 'arbres remarquables' register has other Strasbourg entries (a beech, poplars, planes, a yew) but this specific pine did not surface in it. Flag for the same reason the already-published Great Beech, Copper Beech and Layering Thuja entries on this city page are flagged: register-only, single source. Distinctive visual character (parasol shape, twisted trunk, ivy) and an unambiguously public location make it a strong collectible point despite the missing age and second source. Register total for the city is 66 remarkable-tree entries; this is one of three in Parc de l'Orangerie already represented on the published page (with the beech and the thuja), a short walk from both.
